title: صفقة من العيار الثقيل.. بوتشيتينو يسهل مهمة مانشستر يونايتد لخطف "وريث ميسي"
summary: قال تقرير صحفي، اليوم الأربعاء، إن قدوم الأرجنتيني ماوريسيو بوتشيتينو، إلى مانشستر يونايتد، يقربه خطوة من ضم الوريث المنتظر للأسطورة ليونيل ميسي, نجم إنتر ميامي الأمريكي.

title: 2,000-year-old tomb of an elite nomad in Mongolia contained a Roman glass cup and Han-dynasty-inspired jade decorations
summary: A 2,000-year-old tomb was discovered in an elite burial ground of the Xiongnu, some of whom were the ancestors of the Huns.
body: Archaeologists have unearthed a massive 2,000-year-old tomb of an elite nomad from the Xiongnu Empire in Central Asia. The nine-level tomb contained more than 400 grave goods and is the largest Xiongnu tomb ever found in Mongolia. Archaeologists identified the enormous tomb full of riches during a four-year excavation at the site of Duurlig Nars in northern Mongolia, according to a translated statement from the National Museum of Korea, whose researchers have been excavating the site in cooperation with the Institute of Archaeology of the Mongolian Academy of Sciences and the National Museum of Mongolia. Duurlig Nars is the largest noble burial complex of the Xiongnu Empire, with nearly 300 ancient burial mounds called kurgans. The Xiongnu, also known as the Hunnu, were a collection of nomadic tribes who coalesced into a mobile empire on the Mongolian steppe in 209 B.C. The Xiongnu were connected to a broad trading network that stretched from the Roman Empire in the West to China and the Korean Peninsula in the East. title: Physicists propose new quantum device to measure how Earth twists space-time
summary: A proposed tabletop quantum sensor could match the precision of the best satellite measurements of frame dragging, a subtle effect predicted by Einstein's general relativity.
body: Scientists have proposed a new tabletop device to detect the subtle way Earth's daily spin on its axis twists the space-time around it ‪—‬ an effect predicted by Einstein's general relativity. If built, the sensor could measure the quantum effect known as frame dragging with the same precision as the best satellite experiments, but in minutes instead of years, the researchers proposed in a new study. The research, published Sept. 17 in the journal Physical Review Letters , aimed to address a classic mismatch in physics . Picture a ring of clocks bolted to a spinning merry-go-round. You synchronize each clock with its neighbor around the ring. Then, you compare the last clock with the first. They don't match. "It is impossible to synchronize that collection of clocks when you're in a rotating frame," Kai-Isaak Ellers , a physics graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) and first author of the study, told Live Science.
